title: Black holes
scope: Classical black holes, from the horizon to astrophysics: why r = 2M in Schwarzschild is a coordinate rather than a curvature singularity; radial infall, finite proper time and infinite redshift; tides and spaghettification; the interior where r is timelike and the r = 0 singularity; tortoise, Eddington-Finkelstein, Painleve-Gullstrand and Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates and the null-coordinate technique behind them; event horizons and their global nature; gravitational collapse; the Kruskal extension with its white hole, Einstein-Rosen bridge and Penrose diagrams; Reissner-Nordstrom and Kerr(-Newman) black holes with inner horizons, extremality and maximal extensions; frame dragging, the stationary limit, ergosphere, negative-energy orbits, the Penrose process and Kerr orbits; horizon area, the area theorem, Killing horizons and surface gravity as classical geometry; uniqueness (no-hair) and stability; and astrophysical black holes with their observation. Hawking radiation and black-hole thermodynamics, general causal-structure tools and gravitational-wave signals of black holes are handled in their own domains.

concepts.title: Newtonian dark star
concepts.summary: An eighteenth-century idea that a body compact enough for its Newtonian escape speed to exceed c would trap corpuscular light. Its critical radius 2GM/c^2 happens to equal the Schwarzschild radius, but in the Newtonian picture light still rises and falls back, whereas in general relativity nothing inside the horizon moves outward at all.

concepts.title: Mean density of a black hole
concepts.summary: The mass of a hole divided by the Euclidean volume 4 pi r_s^3/3 scales as 1/M^2, so a billion-solar-mass hole forms at roughly the density of water. Black-hole formation therefore needs no exotic high-density physics for large masses, and the tidal field at the horizon weakens in the same proportion.

names: mean density at the Schwarzschild radius

concepts.title: Coordinate singularity
concepts.summary: A place where metric components in a particular chart blow up, vanish or become degenerate only because the coordinates fail there, while curvature invariants and physical measurements stay finite. It disappears under a suitable change of coordinates; r = 2M in Schwarzschild coordinates and the poles of spherical coordinates are the standard examples.
concepts.notes: Worked examples in the books: polar coordinates at the origin, the polar axis of spherical coordinates, a 1/t^4 toy metric, the Rindler wedge boundary, r = 2M in Schwarzschild, r_plus and r_minus in Reissner-Nordstrom and Kerr, the poles of the Einstein static universe chart, and the Penrose-Khan fold singularities. The diagnostic test is a curvature invariant such as the Kretschmann scalar.

concepts.title: Radial null geodesics in Schwarzschild spacetime
aliases: closing of light cones near the horizon
concepts.summary: Radial light rays in the Schwarzschild geometry obey dt/dr = +/-(1 - 2M/r)^{-1}, so t = +/-(r + 2M ln|r/2M - 1|) + const. Drawn in Schwarzschild coordinates their light cones narrow to vertical slits as r approaches 2M, a distortion of the chart that makes any approach to the horizon take infinite coordinate time.

concepts.title: Radial infall into a black hole
aliases: radial infall from rest at infinity
concepts.summary: A radial timelike geodesic in Schwarzschild with conserved energy per unit mass E; for release from rest at infinity (E = 1) dr/dtau = -(2M/r)^{1/2}, the same form as the Newtonian result. The fall is smooth through r = 2M: the coordinate speed dr/dt goes to zero there while the speed measured by a static observer approaches c.

radial plunge from rest at infinity

The GA ch20 mention of radial plunge as the Newtonian orbit with no angular-momentum barrier belongs with orbits-light-and-tests.

concepts.title: Finite proper time to cross the horizon
aliases: proper time versus coordinate time at the horizon
coordinate-time divergence at the Schwarzschild radius
concepts.summary: An infalling body reaches r = 2M and then r = 0 after a finite proper time (4M/3 from horizon to centre for fall from rest at infinity), yet the Schwarzschild time t along its path diverges logarithmically, with r - 2M shrinking like exp(-t/2M). The infinity belongs to the t coordinate, not to the traveller, which is the first clue that r = 2M is a coordinate singularity.

logarithmic divergence of coordinate time at the horizon
proper time versus coordinate time at the horizon

concepts.title: Interior of a Schwarzschild black hole
aliases: interchange of t and r inside the horizon
r becomes timelike inside the horizon
regions I and II of Schwarzschild
concepts.summary: For r < 2M the metric coefficients of dt^2 and dr^2 swap sign, so r is a time coordinate and t labels a spatial direction; the interior is not static. Every future-directed timelike or null curve must move to smaller r and reaches r = 0 in finite proper time, however hard a rocket fires.

concepts.notes: Includes the division of the Schwarzschild chart into region I (r > 2M) and region II (0 < r < 2M), the fact that time translation is a symmetry only outside, and the norm of the Killing vector xi = partial_t, which is timelike outside, null on r = 2M and spacelike inside (the fact behind negative Killing energy in the Hawking argument). DIV ch19 applies the same reasoning to the region between the Reissner-Nordstrom horizons.

concepts.title: Schwarzschild singularity at r = 0
aliases: central singularity of a black hole
concepts.summary: The genuine singularity of the Schwarzschild geometry, where the Kretschmann scalar 48M^2/r^6 and all tidal accelerations diverge. Because r is timelike inside the horizon, r = 0 is a spacelike moment in the future of everything in the black-hole region rather than a point in space; in the Kruskal extension there is also a past copy bounding the white hole.

concepts.title: Tidal field of a Schwarzschild black hole
aliases: Schwarzschild Riemann components in an orthonormal frame
concepts.summary: In the orthonormal frame of a static or radially falling observer the Schwarzschild curvature gives radial relative acceleration +2M/r^3 per unit separation and transverse relative acceleration -M/r^3, matching the Newtonian tidal tensor. These components are finite at r = 2M and diverge only as r goes to 0.

names: Riemann tensor in the static orthonormal frame
Schwarzschild Riemann components in an orthonormal frame

merged_from: Riemann tensor in the static orthonormal frame
Schwarzschild Riemann components in an orthonormal frame
concepts.notes: A radial boost leaves these particular Riemann components unchanged, which is why the static-frame values apply to a falling astronaut; GA does not spell this out. The pattern preserves volume to first order, as vacuum requires.

concepts.title: Spaghettification
aliases: tidal disruption of an infalling observer
concepts.summary: The radial stretching and sideways squeezing of a body falling toward a black hole, which grows without bound near r = 0 and tears any object apart. A star is disrupted where the hole's tidal acceleration exceeds its self-gravity, at R_T ~ (M_H/rho)^{1/3}; since the horizon grows faster with mass, stellar-mass holes shred infallers outside the horizon while supermassive ones swallow stars whole.

concepts.title: Tortoise coordinate
concepts.summary: The radial coordinate r* = r + 2M ln|r/2M - 1|, defined by dr*/dr = (1 - 2M/r)^{-1}, which pushes the horizon to r* = -infinity and turns radial light rays into straight lines t = +/-r* + const. In (t, r*) the radial part of the Schwarzschild metric is (1 - 2M/r) times flat 1+1 Minkowski space.

names: conformally flat form of the radial Schwarzschild metric

merged_from: conformally flat form of the radial Schwarzschild metric
concepts.notes: DIV ch19 defines the analogous function for Reissner-Nordstrom with dr*/dr = 1/g_00. The name refers to Zeno's paradox of Achilles and the tortoise.

concepts.title: Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates
concepts.summary: Coordinates that replace Schwarzschild t by a null coordinate, v = t + r* (ingoing) or u = t - r* (outgoing), keeping r and the angles. With v the metric -(1 - 2M/r) dv^2 + 2 dv dr + r^2 dOmega^2 is regular across r = 2M, so infalling matter and ingoing light cross the future horizon smoothly; the outgoing version does the same for the past horizon.
concepts.notes: GA ch05 practises on a toy metric -x dv^2 + 2 dv dx before the real one. DIV ch19 builds the Reissner-Nordstrom analogue; the Kerr analogue in (v, r, theta, phi-bar) is folded into kerr-metric.

concepts.title: Painleve-Gullstrand coordinates
concepts.summary: Schwarzschild coordinates whose time is the proper time of observers falling radially from rest at infinity, giving -(1 - 2M/r) dT^2 + 2(2M/r)^{1/2} dT dr + dr^2 + r^2 dOmega^2. The metric is regular at r = 2M and its constant-T slices are flat Euclidean space, which supports the picture of space flowing inward at the Newtonian escape speed.
concepts.notes: The historically first horizon-regular form (1921-22), long misread by its discoverers as a different solution.

concepts.title: Light-cone tipping at the horizon
concepts.summary: In horizon-penetrating coordinates the future light cones lean further toward decreasing r as r decreases. Outside r = 2M one edge still points outward; on the horizon the outgoing edge stays at fixed r; inside, both edges point inward, so no future-directed path can increase r.

names: radial null directions across a horizon

concepts.notes: Common pitfall: a cone tilt drawn in one coordinate system is not a change in the local speed of light, and the tilt alone does not locate the event horizon, which is a global object.

concepts.title: Event horizon
concepts.summary: The boundary of the region of an asymptotically flat spacetime from which no future-directed causal curve reaches distant observers (future null infinity). It is a null hypersurface generated by light rays that neither escape nor fall in; for Schwarzschild it is r = 2M, where curvature is finite but crossing is one-way.
concepts.notes: DIV ch03 first meets a horizon for uniformly accelerated observers in flat spacetime, and DIV ch19 and ch20 locate the outer horizons of Reissner-Nordstrom and Kerr. Cosmological and observer-dependent horizons are handled in other domains.

concepts.title: Black hole
concepts.summary: A region of spacetime from which no signal, not even light, can escape to distant observers, bounded by an event horizon. The simplest, non-rotating and uncharged case is the Schwarzschild geometry continued inside r = 2M, whose interior ends at the curvature singularity r = 0.

concepts.title: Infinite redshift at the horizon
aliases: exponential redshift of an infalling source
concepts.summary: Light sent outward by a source falling toward r = 2M reaches distant observers ever later and more redshifted, the frequency dying away as exp(-t/4M), so the source appears to slow, redden and fade without ever being seen to cross. The crossing itself happens in finite proper time; only finitely many signals are emitted before it.

names: apparent freezing and redshifting of infalling sources
exponential redshift of an infalling source
infinite redshift at the event horizon

merged_from: apparent freezing and redshifting of infalling sources
exponential redshift of an infalling source
infinite redshift at the event horizon
concepts.notes: Folded in: the static-observer factor (1 - 2M/r)^{-1/2} near the horizon (GA ch28), its reverse reading as an unbounded blueshift of starlight falling toward an observer near the hole (GA ch25), and signal delays read from the Kruskal diagram (GA ch27). The e-folding time 4M is the inverse surface gravity. A common error is to say a collapsing star freezes as a visible photograph; it actually fades rapidly.

concepts.title: Teleological nature of the event horizon
aliases: global nature of the event horizon
concepts.summary: Whether an event lies inside the event horizon depends on the entire future of the spacetime, so the horizon cannot be found by local measurements. A horizon starts growing before matter destined to fall in arrives, and in a collapsing star it forms at the centre before the surface reaches 2M.

names: teleological nature of the event horizon
horizon forms before the surface crosses

merged_from: teleological nature of the event horizon

concepts.title: Gravitational collapse
aliases: stellar collapse to a black hole
concepts.summary: The unhalted contraction of a body whose self-gravity no pressure can resist; in general relativity pressure itself gravitates, so beyond a critical compactness support fails. In spherical symmetry the exterior stays Schwarzschild, the surface crosses r = 2M in finite proper time forming a horizon, and all the matter reaches r = 0.

names: gravitational collapse to a black hole
gravitational collapse to a rotating black hole

merged_from: gravitational collapse to a black hole
gravitational collapse to a rotating black hole
concepts.notes: DIV ch20 sketches collapse of a rotating body: asymmetries are radiated away and the exterior settles to Kerr-Newman. SCH ch04 gives the qualitative feedback argument that pressure as a source makes support impossible once p is comparable to rho.

concepts.title: Oppenheimer-Snyder collapse
concepts.summary: The exact model of a homogeneous, pressure-free ball of dust collapsing to a black hole: the interior is a closed Friedmann-type dust universe joined to an exterior Schwarzschild region. It shows explicitly that the surface crosses r = 2M in finite proper time and that the event horizon forms at the centre before the surface gets there.
concepts.notes: The three books mention Oppenheimer and Snyder historically (GA ch25) but do not work the model; the legacy course did (parametric cycloid solution with matched mass). Idealized: no pressure, rotation or radiation.

concepts.title: Maximal analytic extension
concepts.summary: Enlarging a spacetime known on one chart to the largest spacetime with an analytic metric that contains it, so that every geodesic either continues to infinite affine parameter or ends on a genuine singularity. Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates give a partial extension of Schwarzschild; Kruskal's is the unique maximal one.
concepts.notes: DIV ch17 justifies the step by an isometry on the overlap and likens it to analytic continuation in complex analysis. The general notion of extendibility belongs to causal-structure-and-singularities.

concepts.title: Null coordinate reparametrization
concepts.summary: A method for removing coordinate singularities in a two-dimensional (t, r) geometry: build null coordinates from the two families of radial light rays so the metric reads f du dv, then replace u and v by monotonic functions of themselves chosen to make the factor regular. Exponentials give Kruskal coordinates; arctangents give finite ranges for a Penrose diagram.
concepts.notes: GA ch26 demonstrates the method on the Rindler wedge before applying it partway to Schwarzschild; its Exercise 26.4 uses affine parameters along the rays to remove guesswork.

concepts.title: Kruskal-Szekeres coordinates
concepts.summary: Coordinates (T, X) built from exponentiated Eddington-Finkelstein null coordinates, in which the Schwarzschild metric is (32M^3/r) e^{-r/2M}(-dT^2 + dX^2) + r^2 dOmega^2 with r fixed implicitly by (r/2M - 1) e^{r/2M} = X^2 - T^2. Radial light rays run at 45 degrees everywhere and the metric is regular at r = 2M, failing only at r = 0.
concepts.notes: Curves of constant r are hyperbolae (timelike outside, the null diagonals at r = 2M, spacelike inside) and curves of constant t are straight lines through the origin, so t behaves like a boost angle. A margin remark quoted in GA ch27 observes that nobody would have suspected a singularity at 2M had these coordinates come first.

concepts.title: Kruskal diagram
aliases: Kruskal regions I, II, III, IV
concepts.summary: The (T, X) plane of the Schwarzschild geometry with each point a 2-sphere, drawn with 45-degree light cones. The horizons are the diagonals, r = 0 is a pair of spacelike hyperbolae, and the diagonals cut the plane into our exterior, the black-hole interior, a second exterior and a white-hole interior.

names: Kruskal regions I, II, I', II'

merged_from: Kruskal regions I, II, I', II'
concepts.notes: Used as a working tool: an infaller crosses every t = const line up to t = infinity before reaching the horizon, which reconciles finite proper time with the distant observer's endless wait. Region labels differ between books (SCH I-IV; GA and DIV I, II, I', II').

concepts.title: Rindler-Kruskal analogy
concepts.summary: Schwarzschild coordinates relate to Kruskal coordinates as Rindler (uniformly accelerated) coordinates relate to inertial Minkowski ones: each covers a wedge, is singular on its null boundary, and uses a hyperbolic angle as time. Close to r = 2M the (t, r) geometry is literally Rindler space with acceleration parameter 1/4M, so a hovering observer is like a rocket.

concepts.title: Kruskal extension
concepts.summary: The unique maximal analytic extension of the vacuum Schwarzschild geometry: two asymptotically flat exteriors, a black-hole region bounded by a future singularity and a white-hole region emerging from a past singularity, joined across horizons at r = 2M. A black hole formed by stellar collapse uses only part of our exterior and the black-hole region; the rest is replaced by the star.

names: time reversal of the primed universe

merged_from: time reversal of the primed universe
concepts.notes: The second exterior is causally disconnected from ours, though observers from both can meet inside the black hole; its Schwarzschild time runs opposite to Kruskal T.

concepts.title: White hole
concepts.summary: The time reverse of a black hole: a region emerging from a past singularity out of which matter and light can only leave and which nothing can enter. It appears as region II' of the Kruskal extension and as the interior of the outgoing Eddington-Finkelstein extension, and is not expected to form astrophysically.

names: time asymmetry of the Eddington-Finkelstein extension

merged_from: time asymmetry of the Eddington-Finkelstein extension
concepts.notes: DIV ch17 stresses the time asymmetry: Schwarzschild is invariant under t -> -t, but straightening ingoing rays yields a black-hole extension and straightening outgoing rays a white-hole one.

concepts.title: Einstein-Rosen bridge
concepts.summary: The spatial geometry of a slice through both exteriors of the Kruskal extension: two asymptotically flat sheets joined by a throat whose smallest 2-sphere has areal radius 2M on the time-symmetric slice. Embedded in flat space it looks like a funnel connecting two Flamm paraboloids.
concepts.notes: DIV ch18 also shows an alternative identification of the two sheets as distant parts of one universe, to make the point that local geometry does not fix topology. Traversable wormholes needing exotic matter belong to causal-structure-and-singularities.

concepts.title: Non-traversability of the Schwarzschild wormhole
aliases: dynamical evolution of the wormhole throat
concepts.summary: No timelike or null curve connects the two exteriors of the Kruskal extension. Viewed as a sequence of slices, the throat opens from a pinch at the past singularity to radius 2M and closes again at the future singularity faster than any signal could cross.

names: dynamical evolution of the wormhole throat
dynamical pinch-off of the Einstein-Rosen bridge

merged_from: dynamical evolution of the wormhole throat
dynamical pinch-off of the Einstein-Rosen bridge

concepts.title: Penrose diagram of the Kruskal spacetime
concepts.summary: The conformal diagram of the maximally extended Schwarzschild geometry: two exterior diamonds, each with its own i+, i0, i-, scri+ and scri-, a black-hole region above bounded by a horizontal future singularity and a white-hole region below bounded by the past singularity. It shows at a glance which events can signal which.

names: Penrose diagram of the Kruskal spacetime

merged_from: Penrose diagram of the Kruskal spacetime

concepts.title: Penrose diagram of gravitational collapse
concepts.summary: The conformal diagram of a spherical star collapsing to a black hole: the star's interior borders the regular centre r = 0, the vacuum exterior runs out to scri, an event horizon forms inside the star and rises at 45 degrees to i+, and a spacelike singularity caps the interior. No second exterior or white hole appears.

names: Penrose diagram of a collapse black hole
Penrose diagram of spherical gravitational collapse

merged_from: Penrose diagram of a collapse black hole
Penrose diagram of spherical gravitational collapse

concepts.title: Reissner-Nordstrom metric
concepts.summary: The static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat solution of the Einstein-Maxwell equations for mass M and charge Q: ds^2 = -f dt^2 + f^{-1} dr^2 + r^2 dOmega^2 with f = 1 - 2M/r + Q^2/r^2 in geometrized Gaussian units, with a radial Coulomb field. The field energy produces the extra repulsive Q^2/r^2 term, and Q = 0 gives Schwarzschild.
concepts.notes: DIV ch19 derives it with a radial electric-field ansatz F_10 = E(r) and proves a charged Birkhoff theorem (staticity is forced). SCH ch11 notes astrophysical holes should be nearly neutral, so Q is usually set to zero.

concepts.title: Inner and outer horizons
aliases: Cauchy horizon of a charged black hole
regions I, II and III of a two-horizon black hole
concepts.summary: Charged and rotating black holes have two horizons where the radial metric function vanishes: r_+/- = M +/- (M^2 - Q^2)^{1/2} for Reissner-Nordstrom and M +/- (M^2 - a^2)^{1/2} for Kerr. The outer one is the event horizon; between them r is timelike and every sphere is trapped, and inside the inner (Cauchy) horizon r becomes spacelike again and the singularity is timelike.

names: regions I, II and III of a two-horizon black hole

merged_from: regions I, II and III of a two-horizon black hole
concepts.notes: Beyond the inner horizon the future is no longer determined by data given in the exterior, which is why it is called a Cauchy horizon. In Kerr the outer horizon no longer coincides with the g_tt = 0 surface.

concepts.title: Extremal black hole
concepts.summary: A black hole with the largest charge or spin compatible with a horizon, Q = M or a = M, where the inner and outer horizons merge into one degenerate horizon and the region between them disappears. Sub-extremal holes (Q^2 + a^2 < M^2) have two horizons; super-extremal parameters give no horizon at all and a naked singularity.
concepts.notes: Super-extremal Kerr (DIV ch20) exposes the ring singularity, and its extension through the disc contains closed timelike curves. The extremal surface gravity vanishes.

concepts.title: Maximal extension of Reissner-Nordstrom
aliases: Penrose diagram of a charged black hole
concepts.summary: The analytically extended charged black hole is an infinite vertical chain on its Penrose diagram: pairs of exteriors join through a trapped region to regions bounded by timelike singularities, which open through further horizons into new exteriors. A traveller can avoid the singularity and emerge into a different asymptotically flat universe, but never return to the original one.

names: passage to another asymptotically flat region
gravitational repulsion near a charged mass

merged_from: passage to another asymptotically flat region
gravitational repulsion near a charged mass
concepts.notes: Built from Kruskal-type coordinates whose exponential rate is the surface gravity (r_+ - r_-)/2r_+^2, one patch per horizon. Radial neutral geodesics bounce before r = 0 because of the charge's repulsive term (DIV ch19). Identifying exterior copies changes the topology and lets a traveller come back to their own universe. Physically unreliable beyond the inner horizon because of the blueshift instability.

concepts.title: Blueshift instability of the inner horizon
aliases: infinite blueshift at the inner horizon
concepts.summary: An observer crossing the inner horizon of a charged or rotating black hole receives the entire future history of an exterior region in finite proper time, so incoming radiation is blueshifted without bound. Small perturbations are therefore expected to destroy the smooth inner horizon, making the maximal extensions beyond it unphysical.

names: infinite blueshift at the inner horizon

merged_from: infinite blueshift at the inner horizon
concepts.notes: Research-level follow-ups (mass inflation, strong cosmic censorship) are not developed in the books.

concepts.title: Kerr metric
concepts.summary: The two-parameter (mass M, spin a = J/M) stationary, axisymmetric, asymptotically flat vacuum solution describing a rotating black hole; in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates it depends on Delta = r^2 - 2Mr + a^2 and rho^2 = r^2 + a^2 cos^2 theta and has one off-diagonal term g_t phi. It is independent of t and phi, reduces to Schwarzschild at a = 0, and is unchanged only when t and phi are reversed together.

names: inverse metric of the t-φ block

merged_from: inverse metric of the t-φ block
concepts.notes: Folded in: the general stationary axisymmetric line element with an angular velocity function omega (GA ch29), the meaning of the cross term g_t phi and inverting the t-phi block to get g^{tt}, g^{t phi}, g^{phi phi} (GA ch29), the advanced Eddington-Finkelstein (ingoing Kerr) form regular across r_+ (DIV ch20), and the unsolved problem of a realistic rotating interior matched to Kerr (DIV ch17). Legacy pitfall: reading g_t phi off the 2 g_t phi dt dphi term needs a factor of two.

concepts.title: Kerr spin parameter
concepts.summary: The parameter a = J/M in the Kerr metric, the hole's angular momentum per unit mass, which has dimensions of length in geometrized units. A horizon exists only for |a| <= M, so a/M between 0 and 1 is the dimensionless spin, and its sign gives the sense of rotation.
concepts.notes: SCH Exercise 11.38 shows the Sun has a/M much greater than 1, so collapsing bodies must shed angular momentum. DIV identifies J = Ma by comparing the large-r metric with the Lense-Thirring field.

concepts.title: Boyer-Lindquist coordinates
concepts.summary: The standard (t, r, theta, phi) coordinates for Kerr, adapted to its two Killing vectors so that g_t phi is the only off-diagonal component. Their r is not an areal or Euclidean radius: surfaces of constant r are confocal oblate spheroids and r = 0 is a disc of radius a, and the chart is singular where Delta = 0.

concepts.title: Frame dragging
concepts.summary: A rotating mass forces nearby free particles, light and local inertial frames to acquire angular velocity in its sense of rotation. In Kerr a particle with zero angular momentum still moves with dphi/dt = omega = -g_t phi/g_phi phi = 2Mar/[(r^2 + a^2)^2 - a^2 Delta sin^2 theta], which falls off as r^{-3} far away.
concepts.notes: The weak-field gravitomagnetic (Lense-Thirring) treatment belongs to gravitational-waves and its gyroscope tests to orbits-light-and-tests.

concepts.title: Zero-angular-momentum observer
concepts.summary: An observer at fixed r and theta with zero angular momentum, who therefore circulates at the frame-dragging rate omega. ZAMOs serve as local reference clocks near a rotating hole: the energy they measure for a particle with conserved E and L is proportional to E - omega L, which must be positive.
concepts.notes: GA ch29 uses more general circularly rotating observers u = u^t(xi + Omega eta) at fixed r and theta; inside the ergosphere Omega must be positive.

concepts.title: Stationary limit surface
concepts.summary: The surface g_tt = 0 of a rotating black hole, at r_0 = M + (M^2 - a^2 cos^2 theta)^{1/2} for Kerr, inside which no observer or light ray can stay at rest relative to infinity because even counter-rotating light is swept along. It touches the outer horizon at the poles, reaches 2M at the equator, and is timelike elsewhere, so it can be crossed in both directions.

names: coordinate angular velocity of tangential light rays

merged_from: coordinate angular velocity of tangential light rays
concepts.notes: Found by solving the null condition for photons moving only in phi, whose two angular velocities bracket those of any body at that point; one root reaches zero at g_tt = 0. Equivalently the normalization g_tt (u^t)^2 = -1 of a hovering observer fails there. Light from a source at rest on it would arrive infinitely redshifted.

concepts.title: Ergosphere
concepts.summary: The region between the outer horizon and the stationary limit surface of a rotating black hole, outside the hole itself, where the time-translation Killing vector is spacelike. Everything there must co-rotate, but escape to infinity is still possible, and conserved Killing energy can be negative.

names: spacelike Killing vector inside the ergosphere
light-cone tilting in the Kerr geometry

merged_from: spacelike Killing vector inside the ergosphere
light-cone tilting in the Kerr geometry
concepts.notes: Key distinction from the legacy course: the ergosphere means you cannot stand still, not that you cannot get out. GA ch29 summarizes the progressive tipping of Kerr light cones: upright far away, touching rest at the stationary limit, all co-rotating in the ergosphere, all inward between the horizons. SCH ch11 notes compact, rapidly rotating stars can have toroidal ergoregions with no horizon.

concepts.title: Ring singularity
concepts.summary: The curvature singularity of Kerr at rho^2 = r^2 + a^2 cos^2 theta = 0, which is r = 0 on the equator and, in Kerr-Schild Cartesian terms, a ring of radius a. It is timelike and can be avoided, and curves passing through the disc it bounds enter a region with negative r.

concepts.title: Maximal extension of Kerr
concepts.summary: The analytic extension of Kerr across its horizons and through the disc bounded by the ring singularity. Along the axis its Penrose diagram is an infinite chain of exteriors, trapped regions and inner regions like Reissner-Nordstrom, and passing through the disc leads to an asymptotically flat region with r < 0 where the field resembles that of a negative mass and closed timelike curves occur.

names: Kerr Penrose diagram with negative r

merged_from: Kerr Penrose diagram with negative r
concepts.notes: Described by analogy with Reissner-Nordstrom rather than constructed explicitly in DIV ch20; the extremal case has its own axis diagram.

concepts.title: Equatorial orbits in Kerr
aliases: prograde and retrograde orbits in Kerr
concepts.summary: Geodesics in the equatorial plane of Kerr, solved with the conserved Killing energy and angular momentum and an effective potential that reduces to the Schwarzschild one at a = 0. Because of frame dragging, prograde and retrograde particles and photons have different potentials, circular-orbit radii and ISCOs.

names: Kerr equatorial effective potential for massive particles
Killing vectors and conserved quantities in Kerr

merged_from: Kerr equatorial effective potential for massive particles
Killing vectors and conserved quantities in Kerr
concepts.notes: GA ch29 warns that the cross term mixes covariant and contravariant components (u_t = g_tt u^t + g_t phi u^phi), so converting conserved quantities into velocities needs the inverse t-phi block. SCH ch11 factors the Kerr photon radial equation into two potential curves V_+ and V_-, since the Schwarzschild trick of a single squared potential fails.

concepts.title: Carter constant
aliases: third constant of Kerr geodesic motion
concepts.summary: A conserved quantity for Kerr geodesics associated with the theta motion that does not follow from any evident spacetime symmetry. Together with energy, angular momentum and rest mass it makes Kerr orbits fully integrable, and related separability lets wave equations on Kerr be solved.
concepts.notes: Only mentioned (SCH ch11 bibliography). Its origin is a Killing tensor, which the books do not develop.

concepts.title: Principal null congruences
aliases: ingoing and outgoing principal null geodesics
concepts.summary: The two families of null geodesics in Kerr at fixed theta that are the most outgoing and most ingoing light rays at each point, playing the role of radial light rays in Schwarzschild. Coordinates adapted to them, such as the ingoing Kerr coordinates, are regular across the horizon.
concepts.notes: They are the repeated principal null directions of the Weyl tensor of a type D spacetime; the algebraic classification belongs to curvature.

concepts.title: Kerr-Schild form
concepts.summary: Writing a metric as the Minkowski metric plus a multiple of the square of a covector that is null with respect to Minkowski. Kerr found his solution in this form, and Schwarzschild is the case with coefficient 2M/r and l = (1, x/r, y/r, z/r).

concepts.title: Newman-Janis algorithm
concepts.summary: A solution-generating shortcut: write a static seed metric as a null tetrad in advanced null coordinates, complexify r, shift v and r by i a cos theta, and demand real results. Applied to Schwarzschild it yields Kerr and applied to Reissner-Nordstrom it yields Kerr-Newman, although why it works is not fully understood.

concepts.title: Kerr-Newman metric
concepts.summary: The stationary, axisymmetric electrovacuum black hole with mass M, spin a and charge Q, containing Kerr and Reissner-Nordstrom as special cases. It has a horizon when a^2 + Q^2 <= M^2, and by the uniqueness theorems it is the most general stationary black hole of Einstein-Maxwell theory.

concepts.title: Black hole uniqueness theorem
concepts.summary: Every stationary, asymptotically flat black hole of vacuum general relativity is a Kerr black hole, fixed by its mass and angular momentum alone; with electromagnetism it is Kerr-Newman, adding charge. All other details of the collapsed matter are radiated away or hidden behind the horizon.
concepts.notes: Wheeler's hair metaphor and the vase-and-television cartoon (DIV ch20). The legacy course was careful to state the actual hypotheses (stationarity, asymptotic flatness, regularity on and outside the horizon); results with scalar or other matter hair are beyond the books.

concepts.title: Black hole stability
aliases: no-hair relaxation of perturbed black holes
linear stability of Schwarzschild and Kerr
concepts.summary: The expectation, proven for linear perturbations of Schwarzschild and slowly rotating Kerr, that a disturbed black hole sheds all asymmetries as gravitational waves and settles to a Kerr state. It justifies using exact stationary solutions for real holes and underlies the ringdown seen after mergers.

names: no-hair relaxation of perturbed black holes

merged_from: no-hair relaxation of perturbed black holes

concepts.title: Negative-energy orbits
concepts.summary: Where the time-translation Killing vector is spacelike, inside the ergosphere or the horizon, the conserved energy at infinity E = -p.xi of a physical particle can be negative, because it is no longer an energy any local observer measures. What must stay positive is the energy -p.u measured by a local future-directed observer, which for a ZAMO requires E > omega L.

names: negative Killing energy inside the horizon

merged_from: negative Killing energy inside the horizon
concepts.notes: GA ch28 first uses the idea inside the Schwarzschild horizon for the infalling member of a Hawking pair; the Hawking radiation argument itself belongs to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

concepts.title: Penrose process
aliases: energy extraction from a rotating black hole
concepts.summary: A body entering the ergosphere splits so that one fragment falls into the hole on a negative-energy orbit while the other escapes with more energy than the original body. Because the fallen fragment must also carry negative angular momentum, the hole loses both mass and spin.
concepts.notes: Energy that can be extracted is bounded by the irreducible mass, consistent with the area theorem.

concepts.title: Superradiance
concepts.summary: The amplification of waves scattered off a rotating body when the wave's angular phase velocity is less than the body's rotation rate, which draws rotational energy out. For a Kerr black hole it is the wave counterpart of the Penrose process.

concepts.title: Accretion disk
concepts.summary: A rotating disk of gas spiralling onto a compact object: friction, turbulent or magnetic, carries angular momentum outward so gas moves inward, turning gravitational energy into heat that radiates strongly, in X-rays near stellar-mass black holes. Its inner edge sits near the innermost stable circular orbit.

concepts.title: Blandford-Znajek mechanism
aliases: magnetic extraction of black-hole spin energy
concepts.summary: Extraction of a spinning black hole's rotational energy by magnetic fields, supplied by an accretion disk, that thread the ergoregion and horizon. It is the leading explanation for the power of relativistic jets from quasars and is often described as a practical realization of the Penrose idea.

concepts.title: Ergoregion instability
concepts.summary: A runaway in a rotating star that has an ergoregion but no horizon: a negative-energy wave trapped there leaks positive energy to infinity, which deepens its negative energy and makes it grow until the star spins down. Kerr black holes avoid it because the horizon absorbs the trapped wave.

concepts.title: Horizon area of a black hole
concepts.summary: The proper area of a stationary black hole's horizon cross-section, found by integrating the induced 2-metric: A = 16 pi M^2 for Schwarzschild and A = 4 pi (r_+^2 + a^2) = 8 pi M r_+ for Kerr, which halves between a = 0 and a = M at fixed mass. It is the key quantity of the area theorem and, later, black-hole entropy.

names: horizon area of Schwarzschild black hole

merged_from: horizon area of Schwarzschild black hole

concepts.title: Hawking area theorem
concepts.summary: In classical general relativity with matter obeying the null energy condition, the total area of event horizons never decreases. Black holes can therefore merge but never split, and the area of a merger remnant bounds how much energy can be radiated.
concepts.notes: Example from the legacy course: two equal non-spinning holes can radiate at most 1 - 1/sqrt(2), about 29 percent, of their mass; GW150914 actually radiated about 5 percent. Hawking evaporation violates the classical assumption; that and the thermodynamic reading belong to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

concepts.title: Killing horizon
concepts.summary: A null hypersurface on which some Killing vector field is null and normal to the surface. For stationary black holes in general relativity the event horizon is a Killing horizon (of partial_t for Schwarzschild, of partial_t + Omega_H partial_phi for Kerr), which gives the horizon a local geometric characterization.

concepts.title: Surface gravity
concepts.summary: For a Killing horizon generated by a Killing vector normalized at infinity, the constant kappa defined by xi^b nabla_b xi^a = kappa xi^a on the horizon; physically, the force per unit mass needed at infinity to hold a body at the horizon. It is 1/4M for Schwarzschild, (r_+ - r_-)/2r_+^2 for Reissner-Nordstrom, vanishes for extremal holes, and sets the exponential redshift of signals leaving the horizon.
concepts.notes: Its role as the temperature in the laws of black-hole mechanics belongs to quantum-gravity-and-beyond.

concepts.title: X-ray binary
concepts.summary: A close binary in which a neutron star or black hole pulls gas from a companion star into a hot, X-ray-bright accretion disk. When the compact object's mass, measured from the companion's orbit, exceeds the maximum neutron-star mass, it is taken to be a black hole; Cygnus X-1 is the classic case.

concepts.title: Stellar-mass black hole
concepts.summary: A black hole of roughly 5 to 60 solar masses left by the collapse of a massive star, found first in X-ray binaries and now in large numbers through gravitational waves.

concepts.title: Supermassive black hole
concepts.summary: A black hole of about a million to ten billion solar masses at the centre of nearly every large galaxy. Such holes power quasars and active galaxies, have low mean density and weak horizon tides, and grow by accretion and mergers.

concepts.title: Intermediate-mass black hole
concepts.summary: A black hole between stellar-mass and supermassive, roughly a hundred to a hundred thousand solar masses, with candidates in bright X-ray sources and globular-cluster centres. The roughly 150-solar-mass remnant of the merger GW190521 gave the first clear example.

concepts.title: Sagittarius A*
concepts.summary: The supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, about four million solar masses, weighed from the Keplerian orbits of nearby S-stars that share a dark focus. Star S2 shows relativistic orbital precession, and the Event Horizon Telescope has imaged its shadow.

concepts.title: Quasar
concepts.summary: An extremely luminous galactic nucleus powered by gas accreting onto a supermassive black hole, first mistaken for a star because it looks point-like.

concepts.title: Black hole shadow
aliases: apparent angular size of a black hole
concepts.summary: The dark patch on an observer's sky from which no light arrives, because rays traced backwards in those directions fall into the hole; for Schwarzschild it is bounded by the critical impact parameter sqrt(27) M. Around it lensing piles emission into a bright ring; a static observer near 3M sees half the sky dark, and almost all of it near 2M.

names: apparent angular size of a black hole

merged_from: apparent angular size of a black hole

concepts.title: Event Horizon Telescope
concepts.summary: An Earth-sized very-long-baseline radio interferometer that resolves emission near the horizons of M87* (image released 2019) and Sagittarius A* (2022), showing a bright ring around a dark shadow whose size agrees with general relativity.

concepts.title: Primordial black hole
concepts.summary: A hypothetical black hole formed in the very early universe rather than from a star, possibly light enough (around 10^12 kg) to be finishing its Hawking evaporation now in a final gamma-ray burst. Searches have found none so far; they are also discussed as dark-matter candidates.
